results.raw_content: [Back to Search Programs](/search) # Master Informatique — Informatique [Université Bourgogne Europe](/university/universite-bourgogne-europe) Dijon, France2 yearsTaught in FrenchOpen to international students ## About Master Informatique — Informatique Tuition costs 250 EUR per year. Computer science covers the theoretical and practical foundations of computing, including algorithms, programming, software design and the systems that support modern digital infrastructure. The Master Informatique program at Université Bourgogne Europe provides general training across this discipline, without narrowing to a single specialization, and typically covers subjects such as programming languages, algorithm design, databases, software engineering, computer networks and systems architecture. Students in a program of this scope usually build both theoretical understanding, through subjects like complexity theory or formal methods, and practical skills, through project work and software development. Depending on the options chosen within the program, students may also encounter areas such as artificial intelligence, data science or cybersecurity, which have become increasingly integrated into general computer science training. Graduates from this kind of program commonly move into roles as software developers, systems engineers, data analysts or IT project managers, working across sectors that range from technology companies to finance, industry and public administration, and some continue toward doctoral research in computer science. This master's degree is delivered in French over two years at Université Bourgogne Europe in Dijon Cedex, France, beginning in September, with a yearly tuition of 250 EUR. Students entering this program typically hold an undergraduate degree in computer science or a closely related quantitative field, since the program builds on foundational programming and mathematical knowledge before extending into more advanced computing topics. Because computer science combines abstract and applied elements, comfort with both mathematical reasoning and hands-on software development is useful preparation for the range of coursework and project work encountered across the two years of study.
